site.name: Pālāru Museum of Dravidian Temple Arts
site.concept: A scholarly museum of South Indian temple architecture, sculpture, and ritual material culture from the Chola through Nayak periods.

card_pattern: Each module is framed as a carved niche: a sacred-white surface bordered top and bottom by a thin vermilion + gold double-rule, with a small Aum or conch glyph as a kicker above the title. Card titles in Cinzel small-caps with wide tracking; body in Eczar. Where appropriate, a pair of slim vermilion 'pillar' rules flank the card on left and right, evoking a mandapa bay.
design_rules: The site reads as a stepped, polychrome stone composition — tiered headers, dense ornamental bands, vermilion and peacock-blue against sandstone and sacred-white. Empty fields are rare: every section is closed by a palmette divider or lotus seal. Display type is set in wide-tracked small-caps to mimic the inter-character spacing of carved Tamil-Grantha inscription.

pages.title: Pālāru Museum of Dravidian Temple Arts — Tanjavur
pages.content_brief: Hero introduces the museum as a study collection of Chola-through-Nayak temple arts, founded 1962 by the Pālāru Trust on the bund of the old Vadavāru channel. Three lead modules: 'Now on View' (the Chola bronzes gallery), 'Featured Acquisition' (a 14th-century granite Yali pillar fragment from the Vijayanagara workshops), and a visitor-hours strip. Tone: institutional, scholarly, warm.

pages.title: Galleries & Permanent Collection — Pālāru Museum
pages.content_brief: Walks the visitor through the seven permanent galleries: Stone (granite and chlorite sculpture, 9th–13th c.), Bronze (lost-wax processional images), Wood (ratha and mandapa carvings), Pigment (mural fragments from Tirumalai and Lepakshi traditions), Textile (kanchipuram temple silks), Metalwork (lamps, ritual vessels), and Inscription (estampage rubbings from 41 sites). Each gallery is described in 60–80 words with founding-curator notes.

pages.title: Architecture & the Gopuram — Pālāru Museum
pages.content_brief: A standing exhibition on the evolution of the gopuram from the modest dvarapala-flanked entrances of the early Chola period to the towering tiered structures of the Madurai Nayaks. Includes scaled timber models, plan-drawings of Srirangam's seven prakaras, and a discussion of the kalasha finial as both ritual vessel and structural terminus. Curated by Dr. R. Anantharaman, 1998–present.

pages.title: Visit, Hours & Admission — Pālāru Museum
pages.content_brief: Practical visitor information. Address: 27 Bund Road, East Sivaganga Quarter, Tanjavur 613001. Open Tuesday–Sunday, 09:30–17:30; closed Mondays and on Pongal, Deepavali, and Mahasivaratri. Admission ₹40 adult, ₹10 student, free for scholars on advance application. Guided tours in Tamil, English and French at 11:00 and 15:00. Notes on accessibility, photography (permitted without flash), and the on-site reference library.

pages.title: Scholarship & The Pālāru Journal
pages.content_brief: Outlines the museum's scholarly programme: the biannual Pālāru Journal of Temple Studies (est. 1971), the Visiting Sthapati Fellowship for traditional temple-architects, and current research projects on iron-pin armatures in Chola bronzes and on pigment recipes recovered from the Brihadeeswarar mural fragments. Lists three forthcoming monographs from the museum press.

pages.title: About the Pālāru Trust — History & Governance
pages.content_brief: History of the institution from the 1959 bequest of the antiquarian S. Krishnaswamy Iyer through its 1962 founding, the 1987 expansion of the bronze galleries, and the 2014 conservation laboratory. Profiles the current Director, Smt. Lalitha Venkatraman, and the eleven-member Trust board. Closes with acknowledgements to the Archaeological Survey of India and the temple authorities of Chidambaram, Darasuram, and Gangaikondacholapuram.
